note: Meitou only: alms and offerings (the 'Alms and offerings' setting; feature gate by the al_ prefix). Some townsfolk (one personality in seven, never traders or slaves) ask for alms or an offering. Giving takes the cats; the helper's alms effect raises the speaker's faction toward the squad (+1 per 100 cats, at most +4, up to friendly, never allied: LwMod.Favour) and adds the cats to the squad's 'alms' count (titles the Open Hand, the Almsgivers).

say: Okran sees what we give, friend. An offering for his temple?
The temple's lamps burn on what the faithful give. Will you give?
Okran's light needs keeping. A coin for the temple?
For Okran. Here.
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Okran sees it. Walk in his light.
A small light, but his all the same.
For the temple, and the lamps. Take this.
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Generous. Okran will remember this, and so will the Nation.
That will keep the lamps lit a long while.
Not today.
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Okran sees that too. Go on, then.
Another day, perhaps.
Spare a few cats? The tax men took the rest.
The nobles eat well. Some of us don't. A few cats, friend?
Anything you can spare. Times are hard under the samurai.
Here. Get something to eat.
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: ...Thank you. Not many stop.
Bless you. I mean it.
Here. That should keep you going a while.
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: That's... that's more than I've seen in a month. Thank you.
You've no idea what this means.
Sorry. Not today.
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Yeah. Nobody ever does.
Right. Of course.
Every cat buys a blade to cut a chain. Will you give to the cause?
Shackles don't break themselves. A donation for the cause?
For the cause.
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Every bit helps. Thank you.
One more blade. Thanks.
For the cause. Free a few of them.
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: That's a lot of blades. Thank you, friend.
Someone in chains just got a little closer to freedom.
Not this time.
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: The chains don't wait. But fine.
Another time, then.
